citation: Chicago Public Library. "Mayor Buckner Stith Morris Biography."
limitations: Institutional retrospective and a strong identity lead for B. S. Morris; the project preserves it as a candidate because the 1835 record supplies only initials.

citation: Chicago Public Library. "Mayor James Curtiss Biography."
limitations: Institutional retrospective and a strong identity lead for J. Curtiss; not an initials-to-identity bridge by itself.

citation: History of Du Page County, Illinois. Chicago: O. L. Baskin & Co., 1882.
limitations: Late county history reporting that David Brookins sold carriages in Chicago before the family moved west. It does not tie him to the post-office return and therefore supplies only a candidate identity.

citation: Encyclopedia of Chicago. "Biographical Dictionary: D." Chicago Historical Society and Newberry Library.
limitations: Modern scholarly encyclopedia index. Birthplace is kept distinct from the household record's immediate origin before Chicago.

citation: Encyclopedia of Chicago. "Medical and Pharmaceutical Industries." Chicago Historical Society and Newberry Library.
limitations: Corroborates Carpenter's 1832 arrival and early drug business; does not supply a July 1835 household roster.

citation: Illinois Courts. "John Dean Caton." Illinois Supreme Court Justices biographical directory.
limitations: Institutional retrospective. It identifies Caton by full name and legal career; used to corroborate birth and early Chicago chronology, not household composition.

citation: History of La Salle County, Illinois. Inter-State Publishing Co., 1886.
limitations: A competing exact-name candidate whose stated Dayton and Galena chronology conflicts with assuming he is the Chicago letter-list person.

citation: McLean County Museum of History. "Jesse Weldon Fell."
limitations: Institutional biography places Jesse Fell in Vandalia in winter 1834-35; used to reject, not assert, an expansion of J. W. Fell.

citation: History of Mower County and biographies of its pioneers, including Alanson B. Vaughan.
locator: Alanson B. Vaughan and Lansing Township passages
limitations: Exact uncommon-name lead in later Minnesota records. No source bridge to Chicago's 1835 letter list was found, so no migration or household fact is asserted.
